_comment: OIDF conformance test-plan configuration — OpenID Connect Core, Basic
Certification Profile, OpenID Provider (W9).
Placeholders of the form ${NAME} are substituted by
conformance/scripts/render-plan.sh from conformance/suite.env and the
gitignored conformance/suite.local.env, so this file is committed with no
client ids, no secrets and no host-specific paths. The rendered copy lands
under conformance/.run/ (gitignored) and is what the suite actually reads.
Plan name to select in the suite UI or the API:
oidcc-basic-certification-test-plan
with variant { server_metadata: discovery, client_registration: static_client }.
Those two are the plan's ONLY plan-level variants — the suite lists them,
and supplying anything else is refused outright rather than ignored. The
FAPI templates in this directory learned that the expensive way; see their
_comment blocks.
TWO CLIENTS, ONE DIFFERENCE. client and client2 differ only in how they
authenticate at the token endpoint: client_secret_basic (RFC 6749 §2.3.1,
the Authorization header) and client_secret_post (the body). That is the
point of running both — W8 was the first release in which AXIAM could
answer the header form at all, and this plan is its first exercise against
a real relying party. Everything else about the two registrations is
identical, so a difference in a result is attributable to the method.
WHY THE DISCOVERY URL HAS NO tenant_id. W7 made the discovery document
tenant-aware through an optional `?tenant_id=` parameter, and the `address`
and `phone` scopes are advertised only when a tenant is named AND its
organization has sensitive_scopes_enabled. A conformance plan cannot use
that URL. The suite's CheckOauthDiscEndpointIssuer requires the location a
discovery document was retrieved from to correspond to the `issuer` claim
inside it — OIDC Discovery §4.1, which the suite enforces as an
impersonation defence — and a query parameter breaks the correspondence.
So this plan reads the bare well-known URL, and `scopes_supported` will not
list `address` or `phone` even though the organization has enabled them and
the clients are registered for them. The scopes still WORK: the request-time
gate and the userinfo release are tenant-resolved from the client, not from
the discovery document. What is lost is the advertisement. Whether any
module treats that as a failure is a question this plan's run answers, and
the answer is written up in docs/conformance/ rather than assumed here.
BROWSER LOGIN HOP. Both clients are registered browser_sso=true (W3, plan
§4.0), so the suite's cross-site redirect reaches AXIAM's sign-in page
instead of the 401 a non-browser_sso client gets. Without it every
authorization module in this plan is a manual cookie-pasting exercise. See
docs/admin/browser-login-hop.md for the cookie, the SameSite=Lax iframe
limitation and the 60-second PAR window.
description: AXIAM — OpenID Connect Core, Basic Certification Profile, OP
_client2_comment: client2 is the plan's SECOND client under the PLAN-LEVEL variant, which is
client_secret_basic — so it must be a client_secret_basic client, not the
post one. oidcc-refresh-token runs its second authorization as client2 and
sends an HTTP Basic header; a post-registered client2 makes AXIAM ignore
that header (SEC-093: the registration decides) and answer 401.
_client_secret_post_comment: so the block MUST be called client_secret_post. Without it `client` becomes
JSON null and GetStaticClientConfiguration reports a missing `client`, which
is a message about the wrong key.
_browser_comment: There is deliberately NO `browser` automation block here, and this is the
one place in the harness where the right answer is to do less.
The suite's built-in WebRunner is HtmlUnit. Pointed at AXIAM's /login it
fetched the document and stopped: the page it recorded is the bare Vite
index.html with a <script type=module> in it, and every element the
automation was told to fill (`org-slug`, `username`) belongs to a React
tree HtmlUnit never built. `wait id org-slug 15` therefore timed out, and
a failed browser task INTERRUPTS the module — strictly worse than no block
at all, which merely leaves it WAITING with a URL for somebody to visit.
So the visit is done by a real browser instead:
GET /api/runner/browser/<testId> for URLs the suite is waiting on and
drives them in Chromium. Run it beside `conformance-run`; see
This is a statement about the SUITE, not about AXIAM: a JavaScript sign-in
page is what a modern OP has, and the OpenID Foundation expects the
interactive hops of a certification run to be completed in a browser.
